title: Getting-started skill: onboard a session/human to the agents repo + rosary workflow (rsry init, bead conventions, dispatch, known footguns)
description:
User request 2026-07-16: "we should also have a skill to get started for agents". Motivated by a real failure: a session hit the rsry_repo_register identity error, misdiagnosed it as an account-linking requirement, and fell back to `bd init` (banned, ADR-0014) — leaving a bd-shaped store that needed adoption/cleanup. A skill would have prevented all of it.

Ship a `getting-started` skill in this repo (skills live alongside agent definitions) covering:
1. **Onboarding a repo to rosary**: `rsry init <path>` is THE primitive (store + metadata + managed AGENTS.md + hooks + config registration, idempotent). NEVER `bd init`.
2. **The repo-tools footgun**: rsry_repo_register/rsry_repo_list are the hosted multi-tenant tier — they ALWAYS fail on local stdio ("requires user identity"); local registration is rsry init/enable/config.toml. MCP RepoPool snapshots config at boot: freshly registered repos need `repo_path` until the server restarts.
3. **Bead workflow**: search-before-create, close conditions (acceptance_criteria/test command), comment progress, `[bead-id] type(scope): description` commits (Golden Rule 11).
4. **Dispatch basics**: rsry_dispatch / rsry run --once --dry-run first; file scopes set from code reading, not title guessing.
5. **Cross-org caveat**: this repo is user-profile-owned (jamestexas) — org-installed GitHub App webhooks don't fire here; bead-close-on-merge relies on the post-merge hook (`rsry close-merged --local`).
6. **CLI cwd caveat** (until rosary-560953 lands): bead CLI ops are cwd-scoped; run them from inside the target repo or pass --repo, or results are silently empty.

Format: SKILL.md with frontmatter (name, description with trigger phrases like "onboard repo", "set up beads", "getting started with rosary"), following the conventions in this repo's existing skills.

title: Add explicit MCP-dependency (requires) declarations to agent frontmatter
description:
Replace the prose-only mandate in global CLAUDE.md ("use rsry/mache MCP tools") with a structural, checkable declaration per agent. Inspired by eve.dev's agent/connections/ convention (explicit per-agent MCP/OpenAPI dependency declarations vs. free-text instructions).

Scope:
- Add a `requires:` (or similarly named) frontmatter field to agent .md files that depend on specific MCP servers (e.g. rsry, mache, crumb).
- Add a lint check in scripts/build.sh (or a new script) that validates the field: required MCP tool names are well-formed / match a known registry, and flags agents that reference rsry/mache tool names in their body prose but lack the frontmatter declaration.
- Update README generation (scripts/build.sh readme) to surface MCP dependencies per agent if useful.
- Document the convention in CLAUDE.md's "Creating New Agents" section.

Close condition: scripts/build.sh (or equivalent lint target) runs clean and reports the requires: field for at least one updated agent (e.g. adversarial-synthesis-lead or platform-archaeologist, which already reference rsry/mache tools in their descriptions).

comments.text:
Pivoted from the originally-scoped custom `requires:` frontmatter field. Turns out Claude Code's native subagent spec already has `tools:` (allowlist), `disallowedTools:` (denylist), and `mcpServers:` — a custom field would've been documentation-only *and* would fail the repo's own Gemini-strict frontmatter lint. Used the native fields instead:

- Added `disallowedTools: Write, Edit` to the 6 read-only specialist agents (bundle-isolation-tester, dos-resilience-auditor, enumeration-oracle-hunter, observability-gap-auditor, protocol-replay-adversary, trust-root-adversary) — these already claimed "read-only, never patch" in prose with zero enforcement. This makes that promise structural. adversarial-synthesis-lead was left unrestricted since it legitimately writes docs/threat-model/ADRs.
- Added a `**MCP dependency:**` line to all 7 agents' bodies documenting their rsry dependency.
- Added a lint check to scripts/build.sh (`lint_one`, agent-kind only): flags any agent that calls a known MCP server's tool (`rsry_*`, `mache_*`, or `mcp__server__tool`) without a documented `MCP dependency:` line. Scoped narrowly to known server prefixes so it doesn't false-positive on unrelated snake_case code examples (verified against platform-archaeologist.md's retired-CRUMB examples — no false positive).
- Documented the convention in README.md's "Creating new agents/skills" section.
- Verified: `scripts/build.sh check` passes (lint + include-check + readme drift). Negative-tested the lint rule with a temp file missing the dependency line — correctly fails with exit 1.

Nothing committed yet — working tree has the changes, pending user review.

title: Fix false dolt metadata + track beads.jsonl export
description: metadata.json falsely claimed dolt/embedded (dolt_mode:embedded, dolt_database:agents) but the embeddeddolt/ store is empty (0 issues in both DBs) — the real 4 beads live in the SQLite beads.db, which is what connect_bead_store reads. Corrected metadata to {"backend":"sqlite"} and committed a tracked beads.jsonl export (binary beads.db stays git-ignored, rosary-05fbe0). The empty embeddeddolt/ dir is stale bd-era cruft (untracked) and can be removed. Regenerate: rsry bead --repo . export --jsonl --status all --output .beads/beads.jsonl

title: pr-review-kit: resolve threads + re-request review via gh api
description: Add gh-CLI-only (no GitHub MCP connector) coverage for resolving review threads and re-requesting review to pr-review-kit §9.6 and pr-review Respond Mode §S.9, so the reply/resolve/re-request workflow works without the github MCP connector being connected. Uses gh api graphql for thread resolution (REST has no resolve-thread endpoint) and gh api REST for re-requesting reviewers. Gated on the existing Code-addressed + Reply-posted tracking-file discipline.

title: Spike: stand up one persona as a persistent eve.dev service
description:
Exploratory/research bead — NOT a committed build. Investigate porting one always-on-flavored persona (candidates: pr-board, rosary:evolve, watch-pr) into a standalone eve.dev agent with channels/ + schedules/, to solve "nothing in this ecosystem runs without an open Claude Code session."

This is a design/research spike, not implementation, until scope is confirmed with the user — porting a persona to TS + deploying an eve service involves real external-service decisions (Vercel hosting, API keys/secrets, which channel — Slack/Discord/HTTP, cost). Do not deploy anything without explicit user sign-off on scope.

Deliverables for this bead:
1. Pick one candidate persona and write a short design note: what it would look like as an eve subagent (instructions.md, tools/, schedules/ cron), what channel it'd use, what state it needs (maps to rsry bead/dispatch history vs eve's own session persistence).
2. Identify what's duplicated vs. what's net-new relative to the existing Claude Code .md persona.
3. Surface open questions (hosting, secrets, cost, maintenance burden of a second runtime) for the user to decide on before any real build starts.

Close condition: design note committed to docs/ (e.g. docs/eve-spike-<persona>.md) covering the above, reviewed with the user, with an explicit go/no-go recorded as a bead comment.

comments.text:
Design note written: docs/eve-spike-pr-board.md. Picked pr-board as the candidate (read-only, single data dependency, smallest blast radius of the three always-on-flavored skills).

Covers: eve subagent directory layout, what's duplicated vs. net-new (flagged that Phase 2's "join to local worktree" doesn't port cleanly to a remote-hosted service), and 5 open questions (hosting, secrets, cost, maintenance burden of a second runtime, and whether a standing service is even the right fix vs. leaning on Claude Code's own /loop scheduling).

Not closing this bead — per its own close condition, needs your go/no-go recorded as a comment here before any implementation bead opens. My read: only worth prototyping if you want out-of-session notifications specifically (e.g. Slack pings while no Claude Code session is running); if the itch is "I forget to run /pr-board," a scheduled wakeup is cheaper and doesn't add a second runtime.
